gaps.lead: I don't expect the company to make a profit this year, given the economic climate.
gaps.sentence: Given the economic climate, ___ the company made a profit this year.
gaps.hint: don't expect = would be surprised if + past
gaps.explanation: A tentative prediction: 'I would be surprised if + past simple'.

gaps.lead: Darius soon recovered after the operation on his knee and was able to rejoin the team.
gaps.sentence: After the operation on his knee, Darius ___ and was able to rejoin the team.
gaps.explanation: 'Recovered soon' is expressed with the noun: 'made a quick/fast/rapid recovery'.

gaps.lead: 'I've never been to Asia,' she told me.
gaps.sentence: She told me that ___ to Asia.
gaps.explanation: Present perfect shifts to past perfect in reported speech.

gaps.lead: People say the castle is haunted.
gaps.explanation: People say X is… → X is said to be…

gaps.lead: I wish I had never told her the secret.
gaps.explanation: wish + past perfect ≈ shouldn't have + participle.

gaps.lead: We wanted to continue our mountain trek but the weather was too bad.
gaps.sentence: We ___ on with our mountain trek but the weather was too bad.
gaps.hint: unfulfilled wish: would have liked to
gaps.explanation: An unrealised wish about the past: 'would have liked to carry on'.
